criteria.name: Operational simplicity
criteria.description: Nothing to run, back up or upgrade besides a file.

criteria.name: Spatial queries
criteria.description: Bounding-box queries over millions of points without a full scan.

criteria.name: Concurrent writers
criteria.description: Several processes writing at the same time.

options.name: SQLite + R*Tree
options.summary: An embedded, single-file SQL database with an R*Tree module for spatial indexes.
strengths: Zero setup: one file next to the data
R*Tree index answers bounding-box queries quickly
options.fits_when: One process writes and the data fits on one machine.

options.name: PostgreSQL + PostGIS
options.summary: A client-server database with a mature spatial extension.
weaknesses: A server to run, secure and back up
options.fits_when: Several services share the data, or it outgrows one machine.

options.name: DuckDB
strengths: Fast scans and aggregations over columns
weaknesses: Spatial indexing is an extension and less mature
options.fits_when: The workload is mostly analytical scans rather than point lookups.

recommendation.why: gridsnap is a single-user command-line tool. SQLite's R*Tree gives fast bounding-box queries without a server.
recommendation.trade_offs: Only one process can write at a time.
recommendation.would_change_if: Several services need to write at once, or the data no longer fits on one machine: then PostGIS.
